findings.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but is called unconditionally by AdminPermissions.registerListener on ClientRemovedEvent, causing a 500 error and failed client deletion in V2 realms with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled

ClientPermissionsV2 overrides like canExchangeTo, mapRolesPermission, resource, isPermissionsEnabled, and getPermissions throw UnsupportedOperationException on live token-exchange and admin console paths, producing unhandled 500s instead of 403s or correct evaluations in V2 realms

ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) only checks the type-level (all-clients) permission when the per-client resource does not exist, so creating any per-client permission silently revokes an existing all-clients MANAGE grant for that client
Possible NPE in hasPermission fallback path: AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource result is passed to getPolicyStore().findByResource with no null check

AdminPermissions.registerListener gating on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) may skip removal event cleanup if V2 is enabled via a separate feature flag, leaving orphaned authz resources/policies

Test pollution in PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient: test creates roles/composites but @AfterEach only deletes scope permissions, causing 409 duplicate-role errors on re-runs
testViewAllClients asserts FORBIDDEN for clients().create(null), but depending on endpoint ordering a null body may yield 400 or NPE rather than 403
ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but the ClientRemovedEvent removal listener in AdminPermissions calls it, breaking client deletion when V2 is enabled

canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission and other permission-management methods in ClientPermissionsV2 throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of denying access, causing failures in admin endpoints and token-exchange paths instead of failing closed with ForbiddenException

hasPermission(ClientModel, String) only falls back to the all-clients resource when the per-client resource does not exist, so type-level grants are ignored once a per-client resource is created, unlike V1 semantics
The guard getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty() in hasPermission misses policies created via resourceType, wrongly returning false and denying valid all-clients grants
getClientsWithPermission returns resource names (client UUIDs) without validating they resolve to live clients, causing consistency issues with the broken delete cleanup path

getClientsWithPermission runs a full authorization policy evaluation per client resource (N evaluations per call), on the hot path of client listing with no caching, batching, or limit on resource set size

hasPermission(ClientModel, String) performs redundant store round-trips (findByName miss, type-resource fetch, policyStore.findByResource) and a full permission evaluation even for admins with only a plain manage-clients role, multiplying cost across admin console session requests
hasPermission fallback evaluates the type-level resource with all of its scopes instead of only the requested scope, increasing per-call evaluation work and returned permission collection size

hasGrantedPermission re-resolves realmResourceServer() per resource inside the findByType loop instead of batching permissions into a single evaluation request with multiple resources, turning one bulk check into N checks
ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo() throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token-exchange flows for ordinary clients when V2 is active, with no capability flag or deprecation to warn callers

AdminPermissions global ClientRemovedEvent listener calls setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which throws UnsupportedOperationException in V2, causing client deletion to fail at runtime when V2 is enabled

ClientPermissionsV2 methods getPermissions, isPermissionsEnabled, managePermission, viewPermission, configurePermission, mapRolesPermission etc. throw in V2, breaking admin REST clients/{id}/management/permissions endpoints and canManage/canView paths in ClientResource

registerListener cleanup for RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent is now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so with the flag off stale permission resources are orphaned — a silent behavior change

ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) resolves the per-client resource by internal ID only, while resolveClient accepts both internal ID and clientId, so V1 resources named by clientId are not found and migrated realms silently lose grants

canManageClientScopes()/canManage(ClientScopeModel) in V2 grant type-level MANAGE on the Clients resource, conflating manage-all-clients with manage-client-scopes and widening granted authority vs the documented contract

ClientPermissionEvaluator javadoc documents MAP_ROLES_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE from ClientPermissionManagement, but ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles checks AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES — doc/impl scope-name mismatch causing silent permission misses

setPermissionsEnabled in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener calls it unconditionally, causing client deletion to fail with 500 in V2 mode
canExchangeTo / exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of degrading to deny, causing token-exchange permission checks to return 500 rather than 403 in V2 mode
hasPermission(ClientModel, String) has no null check on getResourceTypeResource result, so findByResource(server, null) can NPE when the type-level resource cannot be resolved

hasPermission(ClientModel, String) may mutate the store on read-only permission evaluation if getResourceTypeResource creates the resource as a side effect, and runs a store query on every permission evaluation with no caching
getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is dead code signaling the exchange path was dropped without a replacement
createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy cleanup lambda calls findByName(name).getId() without a null check, risking NPE during test cleanup
AdminPermissions.registerListener listener body has no try/catch, so exceptions from one listener abort delivery to subsequently registered listeners

Duplicate user policy name 'Only My Admin User Policy' across tests in shared realm causes 409 and test failure depending on method ordering, since @AfterEach only deletes scope permissions not user policies

testViewAllClients passes a null body to clients().create(null) when checking 'can't create client', which may be rejected with 400/NPE before authorization and pass for the wrong reason instead of verifying VIEW-only denial
New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope (canMapClientScopeRoles) added to schema and ClientPermissionsV2 has zero test coverage

testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient bundles MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, and CONFIGURE in a single permission, so passing doesn't prove map-roles scopes work; scopes should be granted/tested in isolation

Behavioral change in AdminPermissions.registerListener (now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) has no test verifying events still trigger setPermissionsEnabled(false) when feature is on, or nothing happens when off

No tests for UnsupportedOperationException surface of ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, managePermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions), so admin REST endpoints may return 500 instead of graceful 4xx when V2 evaluator is active
resolveClient clientId-fallback path in AdminPermissionsSchema (lookup by clientId when ID lookup fails) is untested
getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 and its cross-realm and realmResourceServer()==null early-return branches are untested

Positive/negative asymmetry in testManageOnlyOneClient: no pre-permission negative check for listing (findAll), unlike testManageAllClients/testViewAllClients; also missing in testConfigureOnlyOneClient

Unused private getEvaluationContext method and related dead imports (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, AccessToken, TOKEN_EXCHANGE) in ClientPermissionsV2 that will rot and mislead readers into thinking V2 supports token exchange

Triplicated permission-scope-matching loop in hasPermission(ClientModel, String), hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission(Resource, String) should be extracted into a single hasScope(Collection<Permission>, String) helper
LSP violation: eleven inherited methods in ClientPermissionsV2 throw UnsupportedOperationException, giving V1 callers no compile-time signal; V1/V2 split should be along interface boundaries instead

Behavioral change smuggled into a schema PR: event cleanup listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), risking orphaned authz resources if the feature is disabled after permissions were created

hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fragile all-clients fallback: redundant empty-policy check adds a second code path, and it duplicates resource-fetch + null-guard + evaluate pattern instead of reusing hasPermission(String)

PermissionClientTest.onAfter deletes all scope permissions on shared state; manual brute-force delete can conflict with cleanup-registry callbacks registered by createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy; needs a shared teardown helper in AbstractPermissionTest

clients().create(null) in PermissionClientTest.testViewAllClients conflates no-manage-permission with invalid payload, making the 403 assertion brittle; should use a valid ClientRepresentation as in testManageAllClients

Inconsistent instance/static helper mixture in AbstractPermissionTest: createPermission overloads are static but the new createPermission(client, resourceId, resourceType, scopes, policies) remains instance and getPolicies() uses instance client field

ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException and the client-removal event listener calls it unconditionally when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, breaking client deletion (or leaving orphaned resources) under V2
canExchangeTo / exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token-exchange grant evaluation flows with 500 errors under V2

hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) fallback can silently return false when a resource-type 'all clients' permission exists, because findByResource only finds policies bound directly to the type resource and no test covers this combination

The gate in hasPermission fallback is asymmetric: any policy attached to the type resource (e.g., a Logic.NEGATIVE policy for a different scope) passes the gate, making it a poor proxy for 'a permission of this scope exists'

getResourceTypeResource can create the type resource during a read-only permission check (canManage), mutating the store and creating a concurrent-creation race with duplicate/constraint failures and orphaned resources
getClientsWithPermission ignores type-level 'all clients' grants, returning an empty set for admins granted access via createAllPermission, so pre-filtered listings show zero clients

ClientPermissionsV2 overrides canManage/canView/canMapRoles etc. without falling back to V1 per-client permission scopes (MANAGE_SCOPE, CONFIGURE_SCOPE, MAP_ROLES_SCOPE), silently dropping existing V1 client-level permissions when V2 activates
PermissionClientTest.onAfter only deletes scope permissions, leaving role/mapper/scope mutations behind between tests, causing test flakiness due to non-deterministic JUnit ordering

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but is called unconditionally by AdminPermissions.registerListener on ClientRemovedEvent, causing a 500 error and failed client deletion in V2 realms with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled it handles `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` by calling `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` (see modified block in `AdminPermissions.java`). This diff also introduces `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning `ClientPermissionsV2`, and in the new `ClientPermissionsV2` class `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` is implemented as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If `management(...)` resolves to `MgmtPermissionsV2` under this feature (as implied by the V2 classes added here), a client removal event will trigger that unsupported method and cause an unhandled runtime exception during deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 overrides like canExchangeTo, mapRolesPermission, resource, isPermissionsEnabled, and getPermissions throw UnsupportedOperationException on live token-exchange and admin console paths, producing unhandled 500s instead of 403s or correct evaluations in V2 realms

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces ClientPermissionsV2 where several inherited methods (e.g., setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, canExchangeTo, *Permission factories) unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException. This is not purely theoretical: AdminPermissions.registerListener() handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session,...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false). With MgmtPermissionsV2 now overriding clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2, that call will throw at runtime when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, breaking client removal handling (likely propagating as an unhandled exception). While the finding’s mention of “token-exchange and admin console paths” can’t be fully verified from this diff, the unhandled exception risk is directly verifiable for the client-removed listener path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) only checks the type-level (all-clients) permission when the per-client resource does not exist, so creating any per-client permission silently revokes an existing all-clients MANAGE grant for that client

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, the code first looks up a per-client resource (`resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`). It only falls back to evaluating the type-level ("all-clients") resource if that per-client resource is `null`. If any per-client resource exists (e.g., created when adding a per-client permission), the method evaluates permissions only against that per-client resource and never considers the type-level resource, so an existing all-clients grant (e.g. MANAGE on the CLIENTS resource type) can be effectively ignored/overridden for that client once a per-client resource exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test pollution in PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient: test creates roles/composites but @AfterEach only deletes scope permissions, causing 409 duplicate-role errors on re-runs

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient the test creates two client roles with fixed names ("myclient-role" and "myclient-subRole") via realm.admin().clients().get(myclient.getId()).roles().create(...), but the class’s @AfterEach cleanup only removes scope permissions (permissions.findAll(...).forEach(...remove())) and does not delete those roles/composites. If the same realm/client state is reused across test re-runs, subsequent runs would attempt to create the same roles again and can hit 409 duplicate-role conflicts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testViewAllClients asserts FORBIDDEN for clients().create(null), but depending on endpoint ordering a null body may yield 400 or NPE rather than 403

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest.testViewAllClients the test does `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).clients().create(null)` and asserts `Status.FORBIDDEN` (403). Passing a null representation is an invalid request and may be rejected by input validation/deserialization before authorization, yielding 400 (or even an exception) instead of 403. The diff itself introduces this fragile/likely-incorrect assertion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but the ClientRemovedEvent removal listener in AdminPermissions calls it, breaking client deletion when V2 is enabled

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled and a `ClientRemovedEvent` occurs, it calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. The new `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` to unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException` ("Not supported in V2"), and `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`. Therefore, under the V2 permissions implementation, the client-removed listener will trigger this exception during client deletion/event handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission and other permission-management methods in ClientPermissionsV2 throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of denying access, causing failures in admin endpoints and token-exchange paths instead of failing closed with ForbiddenException

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2` class, multiple overridden methods throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (e.g. `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `managePermission`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, etc.). The diff also shows runtime code that calls at least one of these methods when fine-grained authz is enabled: `AdminPermissions.registerListener` invokes `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientRemovedEvent`, and `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. That would surface as a server error instead of a controlled/closed failure mode, matching the finding’s concern about breaking admin paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) only falls back to the all-clients resource when the per-client resource does not exist, so type-level grants are ignored once a per-client resource is created, unlike V1 semantics

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code first looks up a per-client `Resource` by name `client.getId()`. Only if that resource is `null` does it fall back to the type-level/all-clients resource via `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`. If a per-client resource exists (e.g., created for some other permission), any grants attached to the all-clients resource are never evaluated for that client, so a type-level grant can be effectively ignored once a per-client resource exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The guard getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty() in hasPermission misses policies created via resourceType, wrongly returning false and denying valid all-clients grants

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String), when no per-client Resource exists it falls back to the resource-type Resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and then checks policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). That check is performed on the resource-type Resource itself, i.e., exactly where “all-clients” (resourceType-based) grants would be expected to attach in this schema. The diff also adds tests (e.g., PermissionClientTest#testManageAllClients / #testViewAllClients) creating resourceType permissions (no resources set) that would likely exercise this path and fail if the guard ‘missed’ them. Nothing in the diff shows resourceType permissions are stored in a way that bypasses findByResource.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission returns resource names (client UUIDs) without validating they resolve to live clients, causing consistency issues with the broken delete cleanup path

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission`, the code iterates all resources of type `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` and adds `resource.getName()` to the result set without resolving that name back to a live `ClientModel` (no call to `session.clients().getClientById(...)` etc.). This can yield stale/invalid client IDs if orphaned authz resources exist. However, the claimed linkage to a “broken delete cleanup path” is not verifiable from this diff alone (the diff does not show how/where `getClientsWithPermission` is consumed, nor whether cleanup is actually broken).

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission runs a full authorization policy evaluation per client resource (N evaluations per call), on the hot path of client listing with no caching, batching, or limit on resource set size

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission(String scope)`, the code iterates all resources of type `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and for each resource calls `hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)`, which invokes `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...))`. That is an authorization evaluation per resource (O(N) evaluations per call) with no caching/batching/short-circuit beyond per-resource scope check. The claim that this is specifically on the “hot path of client listing” is not shown in the diff (no call sites included), so it’s best characterized as a concrete performance/architecture concern grounded in the new method rather than a verifiable functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) performs redundant store round-trips (findByName miss, type-resource fetch, policyStore.findByResource) and a full permission evaluation even for admins with only a plain manage-clients role, multiplying cost across admin console session requests

adjudication.rationale: The new ClientPermissionsV2 introduces hasPermission(ClientModel, String), which does multiple store operations (resourceStore.findByName; on miss, AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource; then policyStore.findByResource) followed by a permission evaluation over all resource scopes (root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), server)) just to check for one scope. That is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern. However, the finding’s claim that this happens “even for admins with only a plain manage-clients role” is not supported by the diff for common paths like canManage/client/configure/view, which short-circuit on root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) (e.g., canManage(ClientModel), canManageClientScopes(), canConfigure(ClientModel) via canManage).

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission fallback evaluates the type-level resource with all of its scopes instead of only the requested scope, increasing per-call evaluation work and returned permission collection size

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, when the per-client resource is missing it falls back to the type-level resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`) and then evaluates with `new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server)`. That passes *all* scopes from the type-level resource into evaluation rather than just the requested `scope`, and only afterwards filters the resulting `Permission` scopes for a match. This is a diff-verifiable performance/efficiency concern (more scopes to evaluate, potentially larger returned permission collections), not an immediately verifiable correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasGrantedPermission re-resolves realmResourceServer() per resource inside the findByType loop instead of batching permissions into a single evaluation request with multiple resources, turning one bulk check into N checks

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission`, the code iterates resources via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and for each resource calls `hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)`. Inside `hasGrantedPermission`, it calls `root.realmResourceServer()` again and performs a separate `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...))` for each resource. This makes the permission evaluation effectively N separate checks for N resources and also redundantly re-fetches the `ResourceServer` instead of reusing the `server` already computed in `getClientsWithPermission`. This is a diff-grounded efficiency/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo() throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token-exchange flows for ordinary clients when V2 is active, with no capability flag or deprecation to warn callers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that in the new `ClientPermissionsV2` class several previously-supported operations are explicitly made unavailable by throwing `UnsupportedOperationException`, including `canExchangeTo(...)` and `exchangeToPermission(...)` (and other token-exchange / role-mapping permission helpers). If any existing code paths use these methods when `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, this will cause hard runtime failures rather than a capability check or graceful fallback. However, the claim that this definitively “breaks token-exchange flows for ordinary clients when V2 is active” is not directly verifiable from the diff because no call sites / wiring to token-exchange flows are shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions global ClientRemovedEvent listener calls setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which throws UnsupportedOperationException in V2, causing client deletion to fail at runtime when V2 is enabled

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled it handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). This diff introduces ClientPermissionsV2 (wired via MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()) where setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). If the management(...) resolution selects MgmtPermissionsV2 in this feature mode, client deletion would trigger the event listener and throw at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 methods getPermissions, isPermissionsEnabled, managePermission, viewPermission, configurePermission, mapRolesPermission etc. throw in V2, breaking admin REST clients/{id}/management/permissions endpoints and canManage/canView paths in ClientResource

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` return `ClientPermissionsV2` (see `MgmtPermissionsV2#clients()`), but `ClientPermissionsV2#setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` is overridden to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, a `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` triggers `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false);`. If `management(...)` is using `MgmtPermissionsV2` under this feature (implied by introducing/using V2), this will now throw at runtime during client removal handling, breaking expected cleanup/behavior. The finding’s claim about `canManage/canView` breaking is not supported (those are implemented), but the thrown management/permissions methods can indeed break runtime paths as shown by the listener call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: registerListener cleanup for RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent is now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so with the flag off stale permission resources are orphaned — a silent behavior change

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), the event cleanup logic for RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent is now wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. Previously, the listener always called `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` on those removal events. With the feature disabled at runtime, these events will no longer trigger any cleanup/disable action, so any existing fine-grained permission state (e.g., previously enabled permissions/resources/policies) would not be torn down when roles/clients/groups are removed, leaving stale authz artifacts behind.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) resolves the per-client resource by internal ID only, while resolveClient accepts both internal ID and clientId, so V1 resources named by clientId are not found and migrated realms silently lose grants

adjudication.rationale: The diff newly introduces CLIENTS as a resource type in AdminPermissionsSchema and a V2 evaluator. In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String), it looks up a resource by name == client.getId(). However, AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient accepts either internal id or clientId as input but always returns client.getId(), so any resource created through this schema will still be named by the internal id, not clientId. The claim about “V1 resources named by clientId” and “migrated realms losing grants” is not verifiable from this diff (there was no prior CLIENTS resource type here), and the asserted mismatch is not demonstrated by the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canManageClientScopes()/canManage(ClientScopeModel) in V2 grant type-level MANAGE on the Clients resource, conflating manage-all-clients with manage-client-scopes and widening granted authority vs the documented contract

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly documents in `ClientPermissionEvaluator` that for V2 `canManageClientScopes()` should also return true when the caller has permission to `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE` (type-level). The V2 implementation matches this: `ClientPermissionsV2.canManageClientScopes()` returns `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, and `canManage(ClientScopeModel)` delegates to that. So this is not a verifiable contract violation or unintended authority widening based on the diff; it is the intended behavior as described in the new Javadocs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionEvaluator javadoc documents MAP_ROLES_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE from ClientPermissionManagement, but ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles checks AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES — doc/impl scope-name mismatch causing silent permission misses

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `ClientPermissionEvaluator` Javadoc for `canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles` says the check is for `ClientPermissionManagement#MAP_ROLES_SCOPE` / `#MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE_SCOPE` / `#MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` on the client, but the newly added V2 implementation `ClientPermissionsV2` actually evaluates permissions using `AdminPermissionsSchema` scopes (e.g., `canMapRoles(ClientModel)` returns `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES)`). The diff does not show any code using the `ClientPermissionManagement` scope names in V2, so the finding’s “silent permission misses” claim isn’t directly verifiable, but the doc/implementation mismatch is real and could mislead callers configuring permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setPermissionsEnabled in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener calls it unconditionally, causing client deletion to fail with 500 in V2 mode

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `ClientPermissionsV2#setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` explicitly throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (new file `ClientPermissionsV2.java`). Meanwhile, `AdminPermissions.registerListener` handles `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` by calling `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). If `management(...).clients()` resolves to the V2 implementation (`MgmtPermissionsV2#clients()` now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`), this listener path will throw at runtime during client removal, plausibly turning a delete into a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canExchangeTo / exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of degrading to deny, causing token-exchange permission checks to return 500 rather than 403 in V2 mode

adjudication.rationale: In the added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, multiple permission-related methods are overridden to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`, including `canExchangeTo(...)` and `exchangeToPermission(...)`. This is verifiable in the diff and is a concrete design/behavior concern: if any V2 code path calls these methods during token-exchange permission evaluation, it would result in an unhandled runtime exception (likely a 500) rather than a clean deny decision. However, the diff alone does not show any call sites proving that token-exchange checks in V2 actually invoke these methods, so the claimed 500-vs-403 outcome cannot be fully verified from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) has no null check on getResourceTypeResource result, so findByResource(server, null) can NPE when the type-level resource cannot be resolved
matched_golden_ids: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same nullability issue: getResourceTypeResource may return null in hasPermission, and passing that into findByResource can trigger a NullPointerException; it implies the need for a null check/defensive handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) may mutate the store on read-only permission evaluation if getResourceTypeResource creates the resource as a side effect, and runs a store query on every permission evaluation with no caching

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, each permission check hits the stores (`resourceStore.findByName(...)`, and if missing then `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`) with no caching, so the “store query on every evaluation” part is directly grounded in the diff. The claim that `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` necessarily *creates* a resource as a side effect (mutating the store on what looks like a read-only permission check) is plausible given the surrounding `getOrCreateResource(...)` pattern in `AdminPermissionsSchema`, but the diff does not show `getResourceTypeResource`’s implementation, so the mutation aspect cannot be fully verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is dead code signaling the exchange path was dropped without a replacement
createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy cleanup lambda calls findByName(name).getId() without a null check, risking NPE during test cleanup

adjudication.rationale: In AbstractPermissionTest, the newly added helper methods createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy register cleanup lambdas that do `...policies().user().findByName(name).getId()` (and similarly for `.client()`) without checking whether `findByName(name)` returned null. If the policy cannot be found during cleanup (e.g., it was deleted earlier or creation partially failed), this will throw a NullPointerException and can fail test cleanup/teardown. This risk is directly visible in the diff-added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions.registerListener listener body has no try/catch, so exceptions from one listener abort delivery to subsequently registered listeners

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AdminPermissions.registerListener` registers a `ProviderEventListener` whose `onEvent` method has no try/catch both before and after the change; the only relevant change is wrapping the event handling in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...))`. Whether an exception in one listener aborts delivery to other listeners depends on `ProviderEventManager` implementation, which is not shown in the diff, so the claimed behavior cannot be verified from this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate user policy name 'Only My Admin User Policy' across tests in shared realm causes 409 and test failure depending on method ordering, since @AfterEach only deletes scope permissions not user policies

adjudication.rationale: While many tests create a user policy named "Only My Admin User Policy", the new shared helper `AbstractPermissionTest.createUserPolicy(...)` explicitly registers cleanup via `realm.cleanup().add(...)` to remove the created user policy (it finds by name and removes it). So the claim that policies are not cleaned up (and thus inevitably cause 409 due to @AfterEach only deleting scope permissions) is not supported by the diff; policy cleanup is present in the helper used by the tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testViewAllClients passes a null body to clients().create(null) when checking 'can't create client', which may be rejected with 400/NPE before authorization and pass for the wrong reason instead of verifying VIEW-only denial

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest#testViewAllClients`, the test asserts VIEW-only denial for client creation via `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).clients().create(null)` and expects `FORBIDDEN` (see added code near the end of that test). Passing `null` as the `ClientRepresentation` may be rejected by request validation/deserialization (e.g., 400/NPE) before any authorization logic is exercised, so the test could fail or (depending on implementation) pass for the wrong reason rather than specifically proving VIEW-only access cannot create clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope (canMapClientScopeRoles) added to schema and ClientPermissionsV2 has zero test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new client scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and implements logic in `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` to check that permission. The newly added tests in `PermissionClientTest` cover other V2 client scopes (e.g., `MANAGE`, `CONFIGURE`, `VIEW`, `MAP_ROLES`, `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`), but do not exercise `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` specifically. However, the statement that `ClientPermissionsV2 has zero test coverage` is not accurate because multiple new tests clearly exercise V2 client permission behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient bundles MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, and CONFIGURE in a single permission, so passing doesn't prove map-roles scopes work; scopes should be granted/tested in isolation

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`, the client permission is created with combined scopes `Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)`. Because `CONFIGURE` is included alongside the map-roles scopes, the test’s success (adding client-level roles and adding composites) does not conclusively demonstrate that `MAP_ROLES` / `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` are the scopes actually required/enforced for those operations; the operations might be allowed due to `CONFIGURE` depending on the underlying authorization checks. This is a diff-grounded test-design gap rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change in AdminPermissions.registerListener (now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) has no test verifying events still trigger setPermissionsEnabled(false) when feature is on, or nothing happens when off

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes AdminPermissions.registerListener() to only act on RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent when Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) is true (wrapping the entire event handling block). This is a behavioral change compared to the previous unconditional handling, and the added/modified tests in this diff focus on permission evaluation and CRUD flows but do not exercise ProviderEventManager/ProviderEventListener behavior for the on/off cases. A targeted test would be needed to ensure setPermissionsEnabled(..., false) is still invoked when the feature is enabled and skipped when disabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests for UnsupportedOperationException surface of ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, managePermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions), so admin REST endpoints may return 500 instead of graceful 4xx when V2 evaluator is active

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `ClientPermissionsV2` and explicitly overrides multiple `ClientPermissions` methods to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`). `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is updated to return this V2 implementation, so these UOE paths can be reached when V2 is active. The added tests in `PermissionClientTest` cover manage/view/configure/map-roles behaviors, but do not exercise or assert the behavior of these unsupported methods (nor that REST endpoints avoid them / translate them into a controlled 4xx). The claim that REST endpoints will return 500 is plausible but not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: resolveClient clientId-fallback path in AdminPermissionsSchema (lookup by clientId when ID lookup fails) is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new logic in `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient(...)` that first tries `getClientById(realm, id)` and, if null, falls back to `getClientByClientId(realm, id)` before returning `client.getId()` (new method added in `AdminPermissionsSchema`). The added tests in `PermissionClientTest` and helpers consistently create permissions/resources using `myclient.getId()` (UUID) and never pass a clientId like "myclient" into permission creation/resource resolution, so the clientId-fallback branch is not exercised by the diff’s tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 and its cross-realm and realmResourceServer()==null early-return branches are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new override `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` with nontrivial control flow and two early-return branches: `if (!root.isAdminSameRealm()) return Collections.emptySet();` and `if (server == null) return Collections.emptySet();`. The added/modified tests in `PermissionClientTest` and other FGAP tests exercise client permissions (manage/view/configure/map roles) via admin REST operations, but none call `getClientsWithPermission` or explicitly cover the cross-realm case or the `realmResourceServer()` null case. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a confirmed functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Positive/negative asymmetry in testManageOnlyOneClient: no pre-permission negative check for listing (findAll), unlike testManageAllClients/testViewAllClients; also missing in testConfigureOnlyOneClient

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient`, before creating the MANAGE permission the test asserts several operations are forbidden (e.g., `clientResource.toRepresentation()`, `clientResource.update(...)`, `removeDefaultClientScope(...)`), but it does not include a pre-permission negative check that listing clients via `realmAdminClient.realm(...).clients().findAll()` is forbidden/empty due to lack of permission. After granting the permission, it does assert listing returns one client (`assertThat(allClients, hasSize(1))`). Similar asymmetry exists in `testConfigureOnlyOneClient`: it checks view/secret/scope operations are forbidden before granting CONFIGURE, but never checks listing behavior. This is a concrete test coverage gap for newly added fine-grained client permissions logic rather than a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unused private getEvaluationContext method and related dead imports (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, AccessToken, TOKEN_EXCHANGE) in ClientPermissionsV2 that will rot and mislead readers into thinking V2 supports token exchange
matched_golden_ids: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core issue: the private getEvaluationContext method in ClientPermissionsV2 is unused/never called and should be removed. It adds extra related cleanup (dead imports/misleading implication), but the underlying problem matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Triplicated permission-scope-matching loop in hasPermission(ClientModel, String), hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission(Resource, String) should be extracted into a single hasScope(Collection<Permission>, String) helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show three very similar loops in ClientPermissionsV2 (hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String), hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String)) that check whether evaluated Permission objects contain a given scope. However, extracting them into a single helper is a refactor/DRY style suggestion, not a verifiable defect or an important new risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: LSP violation: eleven inherited methods in ClientPermissionsV2 throw UnsupportedOperationException, giving V1 callers no compile-time signal; V1/V2 split should be along interface boundaries instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2 extends ClientPermissions` and overrides a large set of inherited methods to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, etc.). Since `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns this subtype, any code written against the `ClientPermissions`/`ClientPermissionEvaluator` contract can still compile but may fail at runtime if it calls one of these inherited methods. This is a concrete diff-grounded substitutability/interface-boundary design concern, but the diff alone doesn’t prove those methods are actually invoked in V2 at runtime (so it’s not a verifiable defect here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change smuggled into a schema PR: event cleanup listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), risking orphaned authz resources if the feature is disabled after permissions were created

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce the described behavioral change: in AdminPermissions.registerListener, all cleanup handling for RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent is now wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`, whereas previously it always executed. This could leave authz permissions/resources/policies uncleaned when entities are removed while the feature is disabled. However, the diff alone does not prove this is a correctness defect (it may be intentional to avoid invoking fine-grained authz management when the feature is off, and it’s unclear from the diff whether such permissions can/should exist when disabled), so it’s best classified as a concrete, diff-grounded behavior/maintenance concern rather than a verified bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fragile all-clients fallback: redundant empty-policy check adds a second code path, and it duplicates resource-fetch + null-guard + evaluate pattern instead of reusing hasPermission(String)

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` contains its own resource lookup + null-guard + `evaluatePermission` loop, and when the per-client resource is missing it falls back to the “all-clients” resource and adds an extra `policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty()` early return. This is a separate code path from `hasPermission(String)`, which has very similar evaluation logic but does not do the policy-store emptiness check and does a different resource lookup (`findByName` only). That duplication/inconsistency is real and diff-grounded, but it’s primarily a maintainability/architecture concern rather than a verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PermissionClientTest.onAfter deletes all scope permissions on shared state; manual brute-force delete can conflict with cleanup-registry callbacks registered by createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy; needs a shared teardown helper in AbstractPermissionTest

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `PermissionClientTest.onAfter()` deletes all *scope permissions* via `getScopePermissionsResource(client)...remove()`. The cleanup callbacks added by `AbstractPermissionTest.createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy` remove *user/client policies* (via `policies().user()/client()`), not scope permissions. The diff does not show that deleting scope permissions would interfere with those policy-cleanup callbacks, nor any shared teardown mechanism requirement; the claimed conflict is not verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: clients().create(null) in PermissionClientTest.testViewAllClients conflates no-manage-permission with invalid payload, making the 403 assertion brittle; should use a valid ClientRepresentation as in testManageAllClients

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest.testViewAllClients the test does `try (Response response = realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).clients().create(null)) { Assertions.assertEquals(Status.FORBIDDEN.getStatusCode(), response.getStatus()); }`. Passing `null` as the representation can legitimately yield a 400/415 due to invalid payload rather than authorization failure, making the asserted 403 brittle and conflating concerns. The same file’s testManageAllClients shows using a valid `ClientRepresentation` for this kind of assertion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent instance/static helper mixture in AbstractPermissionTest: createPermission overloads are static but the new createPermission(client, resourceId, resourceType, scopes, policies) remains instance and getPolicies() uses instance client field

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a mix of static and instance helpers in AbstractPermissionTest (e.g., static createPermission(ManagedClient, ...) vs instance createPermission(ManagedClient, String, ...) and instance getPolicies() using the injected client field). However, this is a consistency/style concern only; nothing in the diff indicates it causes broken behavior or a substantive review issue beyond refactoring aesthetics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException and the client-removal event listener calls it unconditionally when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, breaking client deletion (or leaving orphaned resources) under V2

adjudication.rationale: In the listener added/modified in AdminPermissions.registerListener, when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled it unconditionally handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. This diff also introduces `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` explicitly throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If the V2 permissions implementation is active for `management(...)`, client removal will trigger this UOE during the removal event, breaking the deletion flow and/or preventing cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canExchangeTo / exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token-exchange grant evaluation flows with 500 errors under V2

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2` and explicitly overrides `canExchangeTo(...)` and `exchangeToPermission(...)` (and related policy helpers) to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. This is verifiable in the new file. However, the diff does not show any call sites or token-exchange evaluation flow that would invoke these methods under V2, so the claim that it *will* break token-exchange grants with 500 errors cannot be confirmed from the diff alone. Still, introducing a V2 permissions implementation with runtime-throwing methods is a concrete risk/compatibility concern if those paths are reachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) fallback can silently return false when a resource-type 'all clients' permission exists, because findByResource only finds policies bound directly to the type resource and no test covers this combination

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when the per-client `Resource` is missing it explicitly falls back to the resource-type resource via `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, checks for policies on that resource (`policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`), and then evaluates permissions against it. Also, the new tests do exercise the “all clients” permission path: e.g. `PermissionClientTest.testManageAllClients()` creates an all-clients permission (`createAllPermission(..., clientsType, ..., Set.of(MANAGE))`) and then performs operations on specific clients (create/delete/list), which would require this fallback to succeed when no per-client resource exists. Therefore the finding’s claim about missing test coverage and silent false return isn’t supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The gate in hasPermission fallback is asymmetric: any policy attached to the type resource (e.g., a Logic.NEGATIVE policy for a different scope) passes the gate, making it a poor proxy for 'a permission of this scope exists'

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when the per-client resource is missing it falls back to the type resource (all-clients) and gates only on `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` (i.e., any policy exists for that resource), not on whether a permission for the *requested scope* exists. That makes the gate a coarse proxy: an unrelated permission/policy (including one effectively denying/affecting other scopes) will still trigger a full evaluation. However, the method still checks returned Permission scopes for the specific `scope`, so this is more of an inefficiency/clarity concern than a direct authorization bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getResourceTypeResource can create the type resource during a read-only permission check (canManage), mutating the store and creating a concurrent-creation race with duplicate/constraint failures and orphaned resources

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel,String), the read-path permission checks used by canManage/canView/etc. call AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) when the per-client Resource is missing (fallback to the "all-clients" resource type). Given the surrounding API patterns in this diff (e.g., AdminPermissionsSchema#getOrCreateResource exists explicitly to create resources), this introduces a likely side-effect risk during can* checks if getResourceTypeResource performs lazy creation. The claimed duplicate/orphan race cannot be verified from the diff because getResourceTypeResource’s implementation isn’t shown, but the diff does show the potentially mutating call happening in a read-only permission evaluation path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission ignores type-level 'all clients' grants, returning an empty set for admins granted access via createAllPermission, so pre-filtered listings show zero clients

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission`, the method iterates resources of type `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` and adds `resource.getName()` to the returned set when the scope is granted. For a type-level ("all clients") grant created via `createAllPermission(...)` (no specific resources), the relevant resource is the schema’s resource-type resource (e.g. the single resource representing all clients), whose name is not a concrete client id. The method does not special-case that to expand to all client IDs, so callers using this set to pre-filter by client id will effectively see no matching clients even though an all-clients grant exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 overrides canManage/canView/canMapRoles etc. without falling back to V1 per-client permission scopes (MANAGE_SCOPE, CONFIGURE_SCOPE, MAP_ROLES_SCOPE), silently dropping existing V1 client-level permissions when V2 activates

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns `new ClientPermissionsV2(...)`, so V2 will be used when that path is active. `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides per-client checks like `canManage(ClientModel)`, `canConfigure(ClientModel)`, `canView(ClientModel)`, `canMapRoles(...)` etc. but does not call the V1 implementations nor check the V1 per-client permission scopes referenced in the `ClientPermissionEvaluator` contract (eg javadoc explicitly mentions `AdminPermissionManagement#MANAGE_SCOPE`, `ClientPermissionManagement#CONFIGURE_SCOPE`, `ClientPermissionManagement#MAP_ROLES_SCOPE`). Instead it only evaluates new `AdminPermissionsSchema` scopes via `hasPermission(...)`. This means existing V1 client-level permissions would no longer be honored under V2, which is a behavioral regression/contract violation introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PermissionClientTest.onAfter only deletes scope permissions, leaving role/mapper/scope mutations behind between tests, causing test flakiness due to non-deterministic JUnit ordering

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest, several tests mutate realm state beyond just authz scope-permissions (e.g., testManageOnlyOneClient removes/adds default/optional client scopes on "myclient"; testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient creates client roles and composite roles). The @AfterEach onAfter() added in this diff only deletes scope permissions via getScopePermissionsResource(client) and does not revert those realm/client mutations. If the managed realm/client are reused across tests (not shown as reset-per-test in the diff), these leaked mutations can affect later tests (e.g., reliance on defaultClientScopes.get(1)), making execution-order-dependent failures plausible.
